eligibility.quote:
Publish String from C++ with arbitrary byte content: ... std::string data;
      for (uint8_t c = 120; c < 130; c++) data.push_back(c); ... UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte

failed_conditions.quote: There is a heavy mismatch here between the message/C++ types and Python types. `string` is 8-bit data which does not have encoding, neither does `std::string`. Message strings *ought* to be UTF-8, but this is not enforced. But Python strings always enforce an encoding. So it is perfectly possible to publish data from C++, which gets mangled when received in Python.

loudness.quote:
msg_info = _rclpy.rclpy_take(capsule, sub.msg_type, sub.raw)
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte

resolution.quote:
having decode mode with `replace` instead of `strict` in https://github.com/ros2/rosidl_python ... it can change the behavior as following w/o `UnicodeDecodeError`.

```
root@tomoyafujita:~/ros2_ws/colcon_ws# ros2 topic echo /topic
data: "Hello, xyz{|}~\x7F��!"
```
